subject: Belgium parliament
title: What If a Country Had No Government for 541 Days? Belgium Tried It

scenes.text: What if a country went 541 days without a government? Belgium did, and almost nothing stopped.
June 13, 2010. Belgians vote, and eleven parties win seats. Dutch-speaking and French-speaking parties can't agree on a coalition.
Months pass. The old prime minister stays on as a caretaker with limited powers, and the regional governments keep working.
The caretakers even commit Belgium to NATO's operation over Libya in 2011.
And the economy? Economists later built a statistical twin of Belgium to compare. The real country grew faster, about 3 percent ahead in 2010.
Not everything held. In November 2011, Belgium's borrowing costs spiked. On December 6 a new government finally took office, 541 days after the vote. A world record.

description:
What if a country had no elected government for well over a year? After its election of 13 June 2010, Belgium took 541 days to form one, a Guinness World Record; a caretaker cabinet with limited powers and the regional governments kept things running.
Economists Daniel Albalate and Germa Bel compared Belgium with a synthetic control and found GDP per capita grew faster than expected, though fiscal clean-up slowed and bond spreads jumped in late 2011.
What should we run through next?
thumbnail_text: WHAT IF NO ONE RAN THE COUNTRY?
first_comment: Counting from the day the old government resigned, Belgium went 589 days without an elected one. How long would your country last?
